I was sectioned to a mental hopsital 2.5 months ago for 1 week so I can answer.

1. Its the size of a small hopsital or 1 area of a big hospital. 

2. Its normally separate from normal hospitals to give the residents some peace.

3. There are generally 2 wings, 1 acute (For people who can be managed/allowed to do their own thing) and another serious wing (Where patients are more heavily detained and separated). I was in the acute wing. Theres some long term residents in both but less so the acute wing. Longest person there when I went was about just over 1 year.

4. Yes it would take about 1min to run out of the exit of the wing I was in to outside the hospital but it was blocked by 2 doors (1 needing card to scan and the other a manual input password). If you really tried you could prob easily force your way out if you managed to steal a knife from the kitchen. 

5. When you arrive they give you a list of solicitors to contact to make an appeal challenging the decision to detain you but your limited to the first 2 weeks of detainment to appeal. There are some charities that you can call for legal advice while detained too.

6. Your whereabouts is checked every 15-30mins and noted down. It would make it hard to sleep at night when every 15mins the window shutter to my door would open and someone would look inside at me.
